text: Confirmed the report: `dayjs.tz()` with a Date/timestamp/Dayjs input is being shifted by the target zone's offset, while the string form is correct. I have a subagent working on the root cause in the timezone plugin and will fix it, then run the test suite to make sure nothing else regresses. ETA ~12 minutes.

Reproduced: the `Z` offset loses a minute when the input has milliseconds. Cause is in the timezone plugin's instance `tz()` method, where the offset difference is computed from a `toLocaleString` round-trip that drops the fractional seconds, leaving a non-integer minute offset (e.g. -420.0043) that truncates to `+08:59`. A subagent is applying a minimal fix and running the timezone tests. ETA ~12 minutes.

Confirmed: the `nl` locale's ordinal function just returns the number with a period, so `Do` gives "8." instead of "8ste"/"19de". A subagent is fixing the Dutch locale's ordinal suffix logic and will run the locale tests. ETA ~12 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: `dayjs.tz(input, tz)` always ran the input through the string path (`d.utc(input)`), which for a Date/number/Dayjs yields the actual instant rather than the wall-clock fields `fixOffset` expects — so the instant got re-interpreted as a wall-clock time and shifted by the target zone's offset. Non-string inputs are now delegated to the prototype `tz()` (which converts the instant into the target zone), matching the string behavior. Verified: Date, timestamp and Dayjs inputs all give `2020-08-07T12:00:00-07:00` with `valueOf()` equal to the original instant; full test suite passes (524 tests, 0 failures).

Confirmed the report: with the weekYear plugin and `en-gb`, 2021-01-01..03 report week-year 2021 instead of 2020, while 2021-01-04 is correct. This looks like the week-year calculation not honoring the locale's week start / first-week rules. A subagent is investigating the weekYear/weekOfYear plugins and the en-gb locale and will fix it, then run the plugin and full test suites. ETA ~14 minutes.

Confirmed: the round-trip through customParseFormat with the zh-cn locale and an `A` token fails, producing an invalid date. The likely cause is a mismatch between how the locale's meridiem strings are emitted by `format` and how customParseFormat builds its `A` matcher. A subagent is fixing it in the customParseFormat plugin / zh-cn locale and will run the plugin and full test suites. ETA ~14 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: the instance `tz()` method derived the offset from a `toLocaleString` round-trip that drops milliseconds, so for fractional-second inputs the minute difference was non-integer (e.g. -539.9957 instead of -540), and the `Z` formatter truncated it to `+08:59`. The diff is now rounded to a whole number of minutes, which is a no-op for whole-second inputs. Verified: `dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z')` → `+09:00`, `utcOffset()` → 540; cross-checked 9 timezones × 6 inputs against moment-timezone with no mismatches, and the timezone tests plus the full suite pass (no pre-existing test regressed).

Fixed. Root cause: the `weekYear` plugin only handled the forward rollover (week 1 in December → year+1) and never the backward one (week 52/53 in January → year−1). For en-gb, 2021-01-01..03 are week 53 of 2020 (weekOfYear already computed that correctly), but weekYear fell through and returned 2021. Added the missing January case (`month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52` → year−1). Verified: 2021-01-01..03 → 2020, 2021-01-04 → 2021, and an exhaustive check over 129 locales × every day 2015–2026 matches moment with zero discrepancies; weekYear/weekOfYear/locale tests and the full suite pass with no regressions.

Confirmed: `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms')` yields an empty duration (`'P'`) while `dayjs.duration(1)` and `dayjs.duration(1, 's')` work. The explicit millisecond unit isn't being normalized to the internal unit name. A subagent is fixing the unit handling in the duration plugin and will run the duration and full test suites. ETA ~14 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: the duration plugin's `unitToMS` table had no `milliseconds` key, so `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms')` computed `1 * undefined = NaN` (the no-unit path worked because it falls back to 1 for unknown keys). Added `milliseconds: 1` to the table. Verified: `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').toISOString()` → `'PT0.001S'`, same for `'millisecond'`/`'milliseconds'`, all units cross-checked against moment, and the duration tests plus full suite pass with no regressions.

Fixed. Root cause: the customParseFormat plugin hard-coded English meridiem regexes (`/[AP]M/`, `/[ap]m/`) and compared the input to `'PM'`/`'pm'`, so for zh-cn — whose `A` token emits the locale meridiem ('凌晨', '下午', …) — the match failed and the parser returned an invalid date. The parser now matches the locale's meridiem strings via the locale's `meridiem()` function (falling back to AM/PM for locales without one), with no zh-cn special-casing. Verified: your snippet round-trips to `2018-05-02 01:02:03`, English AM/PM parsing is unchanged, and the customParseFormat tests plus the full suite (58 suites, 527 tests) pass.

Fixed. Root cause: `src/locale/nl.js` had `ordinal: n => `${n}.`` — a hard-coded period with no Dutch suffix logic. It now returns `ste` for 1, 8 and 20+, otherwise `de`, wrapped in `[...]` so the advancedFormat `Do` token doesn't re-tokenize the suffix (unbracketed `ste`/`de` would have its `s`/`d` eaten by the seconds/weekday tokens). Verified against moment's nl locale for all 31 days of a month: 1ste, 2de, 3de, 4de, 8ste, 11de, 18de, 19de, 20ste, 21ste, 31ste; your two examples give "8ste" and "19de". Locale, advancedFormat and customParseFormat tests pass, and the full suite is green (57 suites, 525 tests, 0 failures).
